catalog_citation: Creissels, Denis. A sketch of Mandinka. To appear in Friederike Lüpke (ed.), The Oxford guide to the Atlantic languages of West Africa. Oxford University Press. Author's PDF, deniscreissels.fr/public/.

catalog_quote: As evidenced by minimal pairs such as ŋ́ ‘I’ vs. ŋ̀ ‘we’ and í ‘you (sg)’ vs. ì ‘they’, Mandinka has two contrasting tones, high and low. Contour tones (rising, falling and rising-falling) are analyzable as sequences of level tones (LH, HL and LHL) associated to single syllables. The downstep that may affect H tones in some positions is analyzable as the trace of a L element underlyingly belonging to the syllable preceding the downstepped H tone. ... The tonal system of Mandinka, like that of the other Manding languages, is characterized by strong restrictions on the possible tone sequences within the limits of various types of units (roots, complex lexemes, words) and by a complex system of tone sandhi. The general tendency is that the non-final tones of non-monosyllabic words tend to remain stable, whereas the tone of monosyllabic words and of the final syllable of non-monosyllabic wo…
sweep_summary: Both title-hits for mand1436 are Glottolog machine misassignments: Bamba 1990 (accent in the tonal system of Odienné Jula = Odienneka odie1238, a dialect of Wojenaka woje1238/jod, East Manding) and Kastenholz 1979 (unpublished Cologne thesis on the prosody of vehicular Jula of Côte d'Ivoire, Dyula dyul1238/dyu). Glottolog's own records say 'computerized assignment from \"dyula\"' and 'autotranslated from Maho's coding system'. Neither is about Mandinka (West Manding, mand1436/mnk), neither is openly available (Bamba: closed DOI at De Gruyter, OpenAlex oa_status closed; Kastenholz: unpublished thesis, no digital copy located), and neither bears on the catalog's 'tonal' coding, which stays on Creissels' sketch (2024) and Creissels 2019 'Tonologie du mandinka du Pakaawu' (both held held by the project; a full-text search for stress/accent both texts finds no 'stress'/'accent' beyond French 'met l'accent sur' and 'accentué par l'effet de downdrift'). No new first-hand stress statement was read in this search of works with stress in the title; catalog record unchanged.org, Google Books (not reachable by automated download), Semantic Scholar (not reachable by automated download), DNB (bot wall) and UQAM Archipel.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim in the extracted text we hold of Creissels' sketch at sec. 2.4, p. 5, as cited; 'stress'/'accent' do not occur in the sketch. (2) Deciding source is a handbook grammar sketch (author's preprint of the 2024 Oxford Guide chapter) by the language's principal describer; a sketch is not the deepest source, but the same author's dedicated 44-pp tonology article (Mandenkan 61, 2019) and the published 2024 chapter were downloaded now to and both confirm a binary H/L lexical tone system with downdrift, tone classes, weight-conditioned contour tones and word-final tone sandhi, with no stress or accent posited. (3) The only better work not yet obtained is the 639-pp Creissels & Sambou 2013 reference grammar (print only), whose tonal analysis Creissels 2019 partly supersedes; nothing in the downloaded material suggests

sources.citation: Creissels, Denis (avec la collaboration de Yaya Dramé). 2019. Tonologie du mandinka du Pakaawu. Mandenkan 61: 3-46. journals.openedition.org/mandenkan/1886
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: p. 5: 'Comme de manière générale en mandingue, le mandinka du Pakaawu a un système tonal analysable sans problème comme basé sur une opposition binaire H vs. B' (minimal pair í 2SG vs ì 3PL); p. 6: automatic downdrift, word-initial tone stable / word-final tone subject to sandhi, 'compacité tonale' in complex lexemes; p. 18: contour tones H͡B, B͡H only on heavy syllables, mora suggested as TBU; 44 pages of lexical tone classes and tone rules for nouns and verbs. No stress or accent is posited anywhere ('accent' occurs only in 'met l'accent sur' and 'accentué par l'effet de downdrift').
sources.note: Dedicated 44-pp tone description of the very variety transcribed in the sketch; downloaded now and confirms binary H/L lexical tone with sandhi and no stress/accent. Should be added to the record's sources.

sources.note: Describes the Manding dialect of Gbéléban, Odienné department, NW Côte d'Ivoire, closest to Braconnier's Samatiguila/Odienné Dioula (Glottolog Wojenaka/odie1238, East Manding), not Mandinka [mnk] of Gambia/Senegal/Guinea-Bissau. Glottolog's assignment to mand1436 is a machine misassignment of 'mandingue'. Its H/L two-tone characterization is nevertheless compatible with what Creissels says for Mandinka proper. downloaded from https://llacan.cnrs.fr/PDF/Mandenkan26/26Kone.pdf; scanned, scanned tesseract fra+eng at 300 ppi.
